claims.text: The nanoparticles contain iron, nickel, chromium, cobalt, and copper.
The initially solid nanoparticles are single-phase high-entropy alloys.
Differences in elemental surface energies and atomic mobilities cause element-specific segregation during heating.
Selective segregation produces localized compositional fluctuations at the nanoparticle surface.
Elements with lower surface energies preferentially migrate to the nanoparticle surface during heating.
Elements with higher diffusivities preferentially migrate to the nanoparticle surface during heating.
Surface compositional heterogeneities lower the local effective melting temperature.
Locally reduced melting temperatures initiate surface melting while the particle interior remains solid.
The high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles will develop early, spatially localized liquid-like surface regions.
Premelting in the high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles will be heterogeneous.
Size- and geometry-matched monometallic nanoparticles will undergo a sharp, homogeneous melting transition under the same thermal conditions.
Uniformly mixed bimetallic nanoparticles will undergo a sharp, homogeneous melting transition under the same thermal conditions.
Five-element and binary nanoparticle systems can follow different rules of alloy phase formation.
Single-phase random-alloy formation can become more likely as the number of atom types increases when free atomic mobility is limited.
The proposed heterogeneous premelting behavior is expected primarily for nanoparticles with high surface-to-volume ratios when surface diffusion is significant.
The proposed behavior may not apply to bulk materials or particles with negligible surface effects.
The temperature, spatial distribution, and magnitude of segregation-associated premelting depend on particle size, synthesis history, and thermal protocol.
Rapid cooling will consolidate the solid solution after heating through the melting regime.
A uniform melting process with neither localized premelting nor detectable surface segregation, comparable to the controls under identical conditions, would falsify the hypothesis.
